name: Metro academic medical center
beds: 1,661 beds, major teaching, five-star CMS rating, flagged safety-net by its Medicare SSI share, risk multiplier seeded at 1.04
story: The biggest TEAM book in the model: about 2,300 inpatient episodes a year plus roughly 1,100 outpatient joint cases, a $101 million target book. Quality sits at the top of the country: hip and knee readmission 3.7% against a 5.8% median, CABG readmission 6.8% against 10.9%, PSI-90 of 0.67, which puts the proxy quality score at 89 and leaves almost nothing withheld. Post-discharge spending runs 6% under the Middle Atlantic pattern, with SNF spend of $4,700 per episode against the division's $5,200, and the HRRP excess-readmission ratios for joints and CABG are both well under 1.0, so every category lands one to three points below target. Track 3 shows about $2.3 million after sequestration, well inside the 20% stop-gain; the risk-multiplier band of 0.98 to 1.10 runs from roughly break-even to $4.8 million, which is the number to respect.
watch: Hip fracture carries the money. Manhattan uses SNF days at 2,300 per 1,000 beneficiaries, two-thirds above the national rate, and the prefilled 50% SNF share with 28-day stays is why the capped, 60%-realized program still takes the estimate to about $4.5 million.

name: Large community system hospital
archetype: Flagship community hospital of a regional system, South Atlantic
beds: 1,051 beds, open-heart program, four-star CMS rating, not flagged safety-net, risk multiplier seeded at 1.01
story: About 790 inpatient episodes across all five categories and up to 770 outpatient joint cases, a $47 million target book. Spending after discharge is 5% under the South Atlantic pattern: readmission spend per episode is $3,400 against the division's $4,500, and SNF spend sits right at the division, so categories prefill one to three points below target. Two surgical signals pull in opposite directions: the hip and knee excess-readmission ratio of 1.18 adds back about half a point on joints, while a colon-infection ratio of 0.37 takes two points off bowel surgery. Track 1 shows about $550,000 after sequestration. Quality is split: readmissions rank in the top fifth, but PSI-90 of 1.17 sits in the bottom eighth of IPPS hospitals, which drags the proxy quality score to 46 and withholds about 5% of the gain.
watch: Patient safety, not cost. Every ten points of composite quality score is worth about one percent of a positive reconciliation here, and the PSI-90 component is the one the hospital controls. A capped, 60%-realized program roughly triples the estimate to $1.5 million before program cost.

name: Metro cardiac and spine hospital
archetype: Large metro hospital known for heart and spine, West North Central
beds: 605 beds, teaching, four-star CMS rating, destination heart and spine programs, risk multiplier seeded at 1.02
story: A reminder that TEAM only sees traditional Medicare. Hennepin County has 61% of its Medicare beneficiaries in Medicare Advantage, so a 600-bed heart and spine center shows just over 400 TEAM-eligible inpatient episodes a year and a $16 million target book. Spending after discharge is 19% under the West North Central pattern, with SNF spend of $2,700 per episode against the division's $3,600 and low readmission spend, so categories prefill three to ten points below target and Track 3 shows about $670,000 after sequestration. Quality is average on both public measures, so the proxy score of 48 withholds about half of the possible 10%.
watch: CABG readmission at 12.1% against a 10.9% national median is the one lever with a surgical signal attached, and spine, the largest line by volume, has the thinnest margin per episode. The capped program adds about $280,000.

name: Growing micropolitan hospital
archetype: Regional hospital serving a fast-growing area, Mountain division
beds: 139 beds, four-star CMS rating, urban under the FY2027 impact file, no open-heart or fusion program in the public file, risk multiplier seeded at 0.97
story: A home-discharge market. Gallatin County uses 430 SNF days per 1,000 beneficiaries, less than a third of the national 1,400, and only 27% of its Medicare beneficiaries are in Medicare Advantage, so nearly every Medicare surgery is a TEAM episode. About 200 inpatient episodes plus up to 340 outpatient joint cases that outnumber the inpatient joint program, a $12 million book. Post-discharge spending is 29% under the Mountain division pattern, so categories prefill seven to fifteen points below target and Track 1 shows about $990,000 after sequestration, close to its 10% stop-gain. PSI-90 of 1.07 holds the proxy quality score to 46, and the county's low dual-eligible share seeds the risk multiplier at 0.97, which is the main downside risk to that number.
watch: The SNF lever barely exists here: the county has two SNFs and one nursing home rated two stars. Readmissions and the quality score are the controllable items, and because the impact file calls Bozeman urban, Track 1 ends after 2026 unless CMS applies its rural census-tract test.

name: Rural community hospital
archetype: Rural hospital in the Ozarks, West South Central
beds: 120 beds, two-star CMS rating, rural under the FY2027 impact file, sole hospital for several counties, risk multiplier seeded at 0.99
story: Eighty inpatient episodes a year, joint replacement and hip fracture only, plus up to 98 outpatient joint cases; bowel surgery falls under the public file's suppression threshold and can be typed in by hand. The spending pattern is SNF-heavy and readmission-light: $7,300 of SNF spend per episode, more than twice the West South Central figure, against $2,900 of readmission spend, less than half the division. The two nearly cancel, so categories prefill within one to three points of target and Track 1 shows about $70,000 after sequestration on a $4.9 million book. Quality is below average on PSI-90, so the proxy score of 43 withholds most of the 10% quality adjustment.
watch: Hip fracture discharge destination. The prefill caps the SNF share at 90% after hip fracture, and the three county nursing homes average 4.7 stars and all sit on the TEAM waiver list, so a preferred-SNF program with shorter stays is realistic: the capped program lifts the estimate to about $190,000 before program cost. Rural status makes Track 2 available from 2027.

name: Central Pennsylvania academic medical center
archetype: Academic medical center in a mid-size metro, Middle Atlantic
beds: 645 beds, major teaching (0.59 residents per bed), four-star CMS rating, not flagged safety-net, risk multiplier seeded at 1.00
story: The one case the public files put over target. About 300 inpatient episodes, led by bowel surgery and hip fracture, plus up to 190 outpatient joint cases, a $15 million book. Spending after discharge is 10% above the Middle Atlantic pattern: readmission spend of $7,000 per episode against the division's $3,900, while SNF spend is half the division and Dauphin County's inpatient rehab spending per capita runs 2.7 times the national rate. Joints carry a hip and knee excess-readmission ratio of 1.12; bowel surgery is helped by a colon-infection ratio of 0.44. Categories prefill up to five points above target. On Track 3 that is a repayment of about $360,000; Track 1 in 2026 sets it to zero. Hip and knee readmission of 6.8% and CABG readmission of 11.7% put the readmission percentile at 23, while PSI-90 of 0.87 scores well, for a proxy quality score of 52.
watch: The clock. Track 1 shields 2026 only; from 2027 a hospital that is neither safety-net nor rural moves to Track 3 with 20% downside, so the gap has one year to close. Readmissions and inpatient rehab use are the levers, and the capped program brings the Track 3 estimate to about −$60,000, close to break-even, before program cost.
